prerequisites: Introduction to differential and integral calculus, linear algebra of vectors and trigonometry.
It is recommended to take the zero-level physics course offered by our university to new engineering students.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the physical principles of electricity and magnetism.
Apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve electricity and magnetism problems using established methods.
Design and carry out electricity and magnetism experiments, interpret the data obtained and draw conclusions from them.
Handle basic electrical measurement equipment and systems for data collection in electricity and magnetism practices.
Select and use appropriate tools and methods to solve electricity and magnetism problems.
Combine theory and practice to solve electricity and magnetism problems.
Knowledge and understanding of the scientific and mathematical principles underlying their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to design and carry out experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Ability to design and perform experiments and to analyze and interpret the data obtained.

Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to the resolution of problems typical of engineering.

teaching_methods: Master theoretical classes, presentations and personal student work, oriented to the acquisition of theoretical knowledge.

Mandatory attendance laboratory practical sessions, problem-solving classes in small groups with direct and active interaction between students and professor, individual tutorials and personal student work, oriented to the acquisition of practical skills related to the course program.

assessment_methods.method: Partial control exams and class participation

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 40% Continuous Assessment (CA) and 60% from a final written exam. Continuous Assessment comprises 15% from laboratory work and 25% from partial control exams and class participation, complemented by programmed assignments. The final exam must be passed with a minimum score of 3.5 out of 10 to pass the course. Oral tests may be conducted to ensure the acquisition of learning outcomes.
